content.text:
This confirms the bug: a single `XMLFileReader` instance is reused across multiple update sites in the loop, so `filesFromThisSite` (a `HashSet` field not cleared between calls) would retain entries from previous update sites, causing files from a later site to incorrectly be treated as "from this site" (so stale metadata from an unrelated earlier update site's file gets merged/overridden incorrectly).

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: e19d0d3207216dd3456613d3e3ea38423a5c3243

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the full history of `XMLFileReader.java` using `git log -p --follow` and found that the field `filesFromThisSite` (a `Set<FileObject>` used to decide whether an existing `FileObject` came from the current update site) was introduced in commit `e19d0d3207216dd3456613d3e3ea38423a5c3243`. The fix commit (`ab32c49df9`, HEAD) simply adds `filesFromThisSite.clear();` at the top of `read()`, so the bug must stem from the commit that created this field without ever clearing it.

(2) The introducing commit declared `filesFromThisSite` as an instance field (`protected Set<FileObject> filesFromThisSite = new HashSet<FileObject>();`), initialized once at object construction, and populated it inside `read()` to replace the previous (buggy) "same update site" check (`updateSite.equals(file.updateSite)`) with `filesFromThisSite.contains(file)`. Since the set is never cleared, it accumulates `FileObject`s across every call to `read()` on the same `XMLFileReader` instance.

(3) `XMLFileDownloader.start()` (core/updater/core/src/main/java/imagej/updater/core/XMLFileDownloader.java:81-98) creates exactly one `XMLFileReader` and calls `reader.read(name, in, updateSite.timestamp)` once per update site inside a loop — confirming the instance is indeed reused across multiple sites. Without clearing `filesFromThisSite`, a `FileObject` seen while processing one update site remains "from this site" when a later, unrelated update site is processed, causing incorrect merge/override logic for files with the same name across different update sites. This is exactly the one-line gap that the fix commit closes.

I'm confident this is the bug-introducing commit; there's no indication of a second contributing commit.
